findings.sourceText: U.S. electricity demand had remained nearly flat for roughly two decades
findings.explanation: Authoritative and contemporaneous sources describe roughly 15 to 20 years of nearly flat U.S. electricity demand before the recent return to growth.

sources.title: After more than a decade of little change, U.S. electricity consumption is rising again

findings.sourceText: Jennifer Granholm is the U.S. secretary of energy
findings.explanation: The Department of Energy lists Chris Wright, not Jennifer Granholm, as the current secretary.
findings.replacement: Chris Wright is the U.S. secretary of energy

findings.sourceText: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory currently estimates that data centers could account for 6.7% to 12.0% of U.S. electricity use by 2028
findings.explanation: LBNL's June 2026 update replaced the older 2028 range with a 2030 reference case and uncertainty range.
findings.replacement: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's June 2026 update estimates that data centers could account for 9.5% to 15.3% of U.S. electricity use by 2030, with an 11.8% reference case

sources.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update

findings.sourceText: that forecast has never been updated
findings.explanation: LBNL published an update to its 2024 report in June 2026.
findings.replacement: that forecast was updated in June 2026

sources.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update

findings.sourceText: A newer analysis puts the 2030 share at only 2%
findings.explanation: LBNL's newer analysis gives an 11.8% reference case and a 9.5% to 15.3% range for 2030, not 2%.
findings.replacement: The newer analysis puts the 2030 reference case at 11.8%, within a 9.5% to 15.3% range

sources.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update

findings.sourceText: Every U.S. data center project is fully funded
findings.explanation: The universal funding claim is broader than the available project evidence and cannot be established.

findings.sourceText: data centers will consume exactly 649 TWh in 2030
findings.explanation: 649 TWh is LBNL's reference case, not an exact outcome; the report gives a 521 to 843 TWh uncertainty range.
findings.replacement: LBNL's reference case estimates 649 TWh in 2030, within a 521 to 843 TWh uncertainty range

findings.explanation: The claim is a universal future outcome that cannot yet be verified and is not supported project by project.

findings.sourceText: The grid is unquestionably the biggest threat to U.S. AI leadership
findings.explanation: The absolute ranking of threats is a judgment rather than a directly measurable factual claim.
